text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 4.7% today as geopolitical risk in the Middle East spiked sharply. Iran escalated military threats and attacks on U.S. installations in the Gulf region, with a third American carrier arriving and a tanker struck in the Strait of Hormuz — the critical chokepoint through which roughly a third of global seaborne oil flows. The IEA's chief publicly warned there is no "credible pathway" back to normal shipping reliability there. When geopolitical risk rises, oil prices typically become more volatile and unpredictable, which creates uncertainty for refiners who lock in fuel costs ahead of time and can face margin pressure.

The stock has been under pressure all week — down 4% over two weeks — suggesting this isn't a one-day shock but rather a mounting concern as tensions have accumulated. Despite refineries running at a healthy 95.2% utilization and oil storage remaining moderate, the market appears to be pricing in the risk that a broader regional conflict could disrupt supply chains or force geopolitical de-risking that weighs on energy demand.
